title: A repo sets its own waiting-page branding: colour and icon
why: Your question, Oct 27 11:37 CDT (cmsg_01DoF7thf3iq2Srr1UsfXgh2RLR9ApAqe47Chyjxe1AwLm, screenshot of degen's blue page): how did the colour get hardcoded; can a repo pick its own?
note: Today (main 43d9af2) the page draws every colour from one field, brand, in its own database, which a session can change with no PR. Its first value comes from claude-settings' docs/design/repo-colours.json, which reads each repo's own app accent (degen: tokens.json's light accent, #0b5fff). The gap: a repo cannot state its page colour in its own files, so a fresh page or a roll-out writes the claude-settings value again. Widened, Oct 27 12:06 CDT (shiv, cmsg_01DoF7thf3iq2Srr1UsfXgh298aGFo8vjqTL5AUirUzSzF, with a screenshot of degen's header): the header's boxed letter gives way to the repo's own app icon or logo where it has one; the boxed letter stays the fallback. The icon is embedded inline (SVG or a small PNG data URI), since the page loads no outside images. Next cloud lane: one branding setting in a repo's .claude/layout-extras.json, waiting-page-colour plus waiting-page-icon (a path to the repo's icon file); skill waiting-page step 3 and lint/repo_colour.py's colour_for read it first, then repo-colours.json; the page's 4.5:1 contrast check stays. Same lane: a check reads each repo's named accent source and reports drift from repo-colours.json, so a repo that changes its own accent is caught (from the c130 outbox, Oct 27). Red first on a repo whose extras colour or icon is ignored. Port: yes, every repo's page. Placed after c130 (triage, Oct 27): both are waiting-page upkeep. Deferred (shiv, Oct 27; build advisor's call 12:45 CDT): it adds a key to .claude/layout-extras.json, whose meaning waiting-page item 29 (re-asked 11:58 CDT) decides. Asked: waiting page item 3.
